neighbours.label: academic discourse of identity-based critical theory (queer, feminist, Black, Indigenous, postcolonial, trans studies): the pole fires on the function words and verbs inside such sentences; the same scholarly sentence shapes in physics, economics, engineering, musicology or philology are silent
fire: Feminist theorists such as Judith Butler and Sara Ahmed argue that gender is performed rather than possessed.
Critical race scholars, including Kimberlé Crenshaw and Patricia Hill Collins, developed intersectionality to analyze overlapping oppressions.
Queer of color critique refuses the assumption that sexuality can be studied apart from race and class.
Indigenous studies challenges the settler framing of sovereignty and reclaims relational understandings of land.
Trans studies interrogates the medical categories that have been used to regulate gendered bodies.
Postcolonial feminists criticized Western scholarship for homogenizing the experiences of Third World women.
Black lesbian writers such as Cheryl Clarke and Barbara Smith insisted that the politics of identity were inseparable from literary form.
Chicana theorists reframed the borderlands as a site of hybrid identity and resistance to assimilation.
quiet: Monetary theorists such as Milton Friedman and Anna Schwartz argue that inflation is always a monetary phenomenon.
Structural engineers, including Fazlur Khan and Leslie Robertson, developed the tubular frame to resist wind loads.
Plate tectonics refuses the assumption that continents are fixed and explains earthquakes as boundary slip.
Agronomy studies challenge the assumption that higher nitrogen always raises yields.
Immunology interrogates the molecular signals that regulate inflammation.
Classical philologists criticized the new edition for homogenizing the manuscript variants.
Baroque composers such as Corelli and Vivaldi insisted that the concerto's form followed from its ritornello.
Glaciologists reframed the ice shelf as a site of rapid melting and retreat.
